notable_absence.finding: The page's Multi-Document ACID Transactions section is exactly one short paragraph with no code example, entirely deferring to concept-docs/transactions.md - despite the page's own title ('Data Modelling, Durability, and Consistency') foregrounding transactions as a headline topic. It never states the relationship between the KV-level durabilityLevel option described earlier on the SAME page and the transaction-scoped durability level described on the linked page - the sharesOptionSetWith link between sdk:durability and sdk:transaction-durability (established in round 4) is not itself drawn anywhere on this page, even though both concepts are one section apart.

cross_component_finding: This page confirms sdk:durability (client option) and durability:level (the general Server concept it wraps) describe the identical three-level enum from two sides of the same fence - the page's own prose ('levels of durability can be set, to ensure replication and/or persistence to disks, before the write is committed') is indistinguishable from a description of the Server concept, differing only in that it is voiced from the SDK caller's side. Separately, this page draws a genuinely new distinction not previously captured in the batch: sdk:cas-optimistic-locking (the recommended default) and sdk:pessimistic-locking (get-and-lock/unlock, the explicit fallback) are presented as a closed CONFIGURATION CHOICE for concurrency control, not as two unrelated mechanisms - captured here via offersConfigurationChoice.
cross_product_finding: Preferred Server Group Replica Reads is a Capella-cost-driven SDK feature: the page's own justification is AWS cross-AZ egress-charge avoidance ('egress charges for reads from other Availability Zones (AZ) in AWS can be a significant cost'), tying a client read-path API decision directly to Capella billing economics rather than to a pure correctness or availability concern. This is a different kind of cross-product motivation than the Server-version/NTP prerequisite divergence round 4 found on the transactions howto page - here the DRIVER of the feature's existence is cost, and the durability trade-off (favoring persistToMajority to compensate for AZ-local replica staleness) is offered as the mitigation, not the goal.
